entries.clue: Bit of beer and a nut (4)

blocks.note: the froth sitting on top of a poured pint
nut as slang for the top of the body, as in 'use your nut'

annotation.surface: A pub snack order: a drop of beer and a nut to go with it.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface serves up bar snacks, so 'nut' reads as a peanut; it is slang for the head.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are plain senses of one word: the foam topping a pint, and the slang nut for the skull.

entries.clue: Bad luck that’s likely to grate? (4,6)

blocks.note: a British idiom of mock sympathy, said to someone unlucky
a firm kitchen staple such as Parmesan, the kind you grate

annotation.surface: Misfortune described as something that grates on you.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grate' pretends to mean irritate, fitting bad luck; the question mark flags that it is literal kitchen grating of a hard cheese.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Hard cheese!' is a British phrase meaning tough luck.

entries.clue: Commercial to liken Luxembourg to last thing in luxury – well enough! (10)

final letter of luxury

entries.clue: They mean the same thing (5,5)

reads as agreement; really the literal repeat of the line above in a list

annotation.walkthrough: The clue sounds like it describes synonyms or people in agreement; literally, ditto marks signify 'the same thing' in a list.

entries.clue: Splashy, tinselly, less large: so trendy (2,5)

anagram indicator

annotation.walkthrough: 'Splashy' looks like another adjective in the list of descriptions; it is the instruction to rearrange.

entries.clue: Adapts Swift etc for the audience (7)

annotation.definitionFit: To tailor something is to adapt it to a purpose.

entries.clue: The writer, funny character, to cover dirty old men in intros: great note! (11)

first letters of dirty, old, men

annotation.surface: A writer's jumble of notes about a comic character and some grubby old men, ending with a triumphant 'great note!'
annotation.walkthrough: 'Note' here means fame or distinction, as in a person of note; 'great note' is the highest fame.
annotation.definitionFit: Megastardom is the greatest degree of fame, and note means eminence.

entries.clue: Positive review of DJ’s gig (4)

annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one review of one gig, but the two halves are separate definitions of the same word.

entries.clue: Lover-boy rises, inflamed? (4)

entries.clue: In the lecture hall, study example of pond flora (4)

entries.clue: Cambodia’s king overtly to embrace act of invitation (6,4)

entries.clue: Yes, you: all bets are off (10)

anagram indicator

annotation.walkthrough: 'All bets are off' is a set phrase, which hides that 'all bets' is part of the fodder with 'you'.

entries.clue: Old flame, slippery sort, heading off to scold and enrage (10)

annotation.walkthrough: 'Slippery sort' reads as a dishonest ex; it is a snake. 'Heading off' reads as leaving, but it beheads BERATE.

entries.clue: Excerpt of text remembered in the end (7)

entries.clue: Basis of a speech? (7)

annotation.walkthrough: 'Basis' suggests the ideas behind a speech; it is what the speaker physically stands on.
annotation.definitionFit: A soapbox is the crate an open-air speaker stands on, so it lies at the base of the speech.
